summary: Add alternatives coverage metrics and alert
pull_request_body: Issue #2950: the alternatives check ran about 34 times in 14 days and searched about 4 times, and no metric, alert or panel showed it. The owner saw it in the Firecrawl usage. #2946 (merged) now makes the check search before a verdict, but nothing proves that it does. This change makes the coverage and the search activity of the check visible: how many open items have no check, how old the oldest check is, how many searches each written check ran, and an alert for three days with no search.
why: Issue #2950: the alternatives check ran about 34 times in 14 days and searched about 4 times, and no metric, alert or panel showed it. The owner saw it in the Firecrawl usage. #2946 (merged) now makes the check search before a verdict, but nothing proves that it does. This change makes the coverage and the search activity of the check visible: how many open items have no check, how old the oldest check is, how many searches each written check ran, and an alert for three days with no search.
what_changes: Declare the three alternatives instruments in `src/devops_cli/telemetry/instruments.py`.
Measure the coverage of a round in `src/devops_cli/roadmap/alternatives.py`.
Record the coverage in the Service row in `src/devops_cli/roadmap/run.py`.
Observe the searches of each written check in `src/devops_cli/roadmap/alternatives.py`.
Add the alert `RoadmapServiceAlternativesNotSearching` in `k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml` and promtool cases in `tests/fixtures/prometheus_rules/roadmap_service_activity_tests.yaml`.
Add the Alternatives Check row in `k8s/monitoring/dashboards/devops-cli.json`.
feasibility: The module declares and sends instruments as the issue says. `git grep -n "class InstrumentKind" -A4 src/devops_cli/telemetry/instruments.py` shows `COUNTER`, `GAUGE`, `HISTOGRAM`. `ROADMAP_ALTERNATIVES_TOTAL` is at `instruments.py:243`, and `emit` at `:491` calls `record_gauge` for a gauge and `record_histogram` for a histogram. `git grep -n "alternatives_unchecked\|alternatives_oldest\|alternatives_searches" -- . ':!openspec/changes'` printed nothing: the names are free.

The job records one metric today. `alternatives.py:905` is `emit(ROADMAP_ALTERNATIVES_TOTAL, 1, {"verdict": check.verdict.value})`, in `apply_alternatives`, after `store.comment(...)`. `grep -rn "emit(" src/devops_cli/roadmap/*.py` shows no other emit in the check.

The search count is observable. `AlternativesTools.search_web` appends the query to `self.queries` before it calls Firecrawl (`alternatives.py:259`), so a refused search counts. `validate_reply` copies the list with `queries=_clean(tools.queries, allowed)` (`:767`), and `_clean` keeps one text for each text. So `len(check.queries)` is the number of searches that the tools ran. `_skip_check` sets `queries=()` (`:741`): a skip-class check runs no search and has the count 0. `_refusal` refuses the verdict `not-applicable` from the model (`:573-579`), so only a skip-class check has that verdict.

The gauge values are not in the plan today. `select_items` (`alternatives.py:497-527`) builds `unchecked`, `due` and `current`, skips an item in the retry delay with `continue` before it reads the check time (`:516`), and returns `ordered[:limit]` and `current`. The count and the oldest check need the whole eligible set, so `Selection` needs a new field. For `--item N` the function returns at `:509` without a scan.

The row cannot record the gauges after `apply_alternatives`. The adapter at `run.py:608-621` calls `apply_alternatives` only `if plan.has_writes`, and a round with no item to check has no writes. `plan_alternatives` returns `AlternativesPlan(repo=repo, off_reason=...)` at once when the check is off (`alternatives.py:846-847`).

The Firecrawl counter has a different label set from the gauge. `sed -n 843,848p k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml` gives `devops_cli_firecrawl_searches_total{job="roadmap-service", result=~"402|429"}` in `RoadmapServiceFirecrawlRefused`. The counter has the label `result` (`common_tools.py:48,72`: `ok`, a status, or `error`). The new gauge has `repo`. Refine searches through the same function (`refine_investigation.py:268` calls `cited_web_search`, which calls `firecrawl_search`), so the counter holds the searches of every job.

The alert expression of the issue does not fire. I downloaded promtool 3.15.1 (the version of `src/devops_cli/tools_lock/tools.lock`, SHA-256 `6a726885...d97a84` matches) and ran a unit test with the real label sets. Series: `devops_cli_firecrawl_searches_total{job="roadmap-service", instance="roadmap-service", result="402"}` flat at 2, and `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items{job="roadmap-service", instance="roadmap-service", repo="example/app"}` at 2, for 150 hours. The rule `increase(devops_cli_firecrawl_searches_total{job="roadmap-service"}[3d]) == 0 and devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items{job="roadmap-service"} > 0` gave no alert, because `and` needs equal label sets. The rule of design.md (`sum by (repo) (last_over_time(<gauge>[7d])) > 0 and on() (sum(<count of searches in 3d>) or vector(0)) == 0`) fired with `repo="example/app"`.

The six cases of the fixed rule pass in promtool 3.15.1 (`promtool test rules unit.yaml` printed `SUCCESS`, `promtool check rules` printed `SUCCESS: 2 rules found`): a flat `402` series and no `ok` search fires; an `ok` search one day before is quiet; no search series at all fires; a gauge of 0 is quiet; a new `ok` series that starts 10 hours before and holds 3 searches is quiet; a search of `job="devops-cli"` does not count, and a gauge sample 100 hours old still fires while one 180 hours old does not. The same new-series case with plain `sum(increase(...[3d])) or vector(0)` fired (`got: Labels:{alertname="Incr", repo="example/app", severity="warning"}`), so the rule needs the form of `_window_count` (#2505).

The repository tests accept the shapes. `tests/prometheus/test_k8s_monitoring_alerting.py` pins the rule list of the group (`ROADMAP_SERVICE_ACTIVITY_RULES`, `:903`), the whole alert list (`test_the_baseline_rule_set`, `:248`) and `SERVED_SERIES` (`:96`), which has `FIRECRAWL_SEARCHES_TOTAL.name` and none of the new gauges. It also needs each `devops_cli_` selector of the group to have `job="roadmap-service"`, a `for`, a severity, and `(k8s/README.md, Roadmap service)` in the description, with the alert name in that section. Group 5 does each. `promtool` is not on this session's PATH, so these tests skip the live part here; CI installs it.

The dashboard has no Roadmap dashboard. `ls k8s/monitoring/dashboards` lists 15 files. `grep -il roadmap k8s/monitoring/dashboards/*` finds `ai-spend.json` (a panel of gateway callers) and `project-metrics.json` (items and traffic). `devops-cli.json` is titled `devops-cli Telemetry` (uid `devops-cli-telemetry`) and has six rows, among them "Sub-commands", "RAG Retrieval" and "GitHub API"; its last panel has `gridPos.y` 86 and `h` 8. `uv run devops ci test tests/telemetry/test_telemetry_instruments.py` printed `49 passed` on the base: its dashboard checks (a query names a sent series, a gauge is read through `last_over_time`, a histogram through `rate`, `increase` or `last_over_time`) run over `devops-cli.json` and will cover the new row once the instruments exist.

A gauge needs the window in the alert. `docs/TELEMETRY.md` says: "Prometheus finds a plain selector only within five minutes of a sample". The row runs every 719 minutes (`DEFAULT_ROADMAP_ALTERNATIVES_INTERVAL_MINUTES`), so the alert reads the gauge through `last_over_time(...[7d])`.

Rechecked at the implement step on `origin/main` 5bc50d0a: the code paths, line numbers and instrument names above still hold, #2947 is merged (`select_items` takes `first_pass_limit`, and `Coverage` stays outside that logic), and #2919 is merged (`ROADMAP_ITEM_AGE` and the group `roadmap-service-items` exist, so the new names do not collide). `devops-cli.json` now ends at `gridPos.y` 128 with the id 48, so the row has the id 49 and `y` 136. The dashboard test `test_every_panel_counting_with_increase_states_its_limits` requires the histogram panel to state the limits of `increase()`.

Not verified: how a real Prometheus stores the OTLP gauge of a Service pod after a restart, and the value of the live gauges. No collector or cluster is reachable from this session. The promtool cases feed the label sets that `docs/TELEMETRY.md` describes (`job` and `instance` from the resource, the attributes as labels).
existing_tool: Prometheus, promtool and Grafana cover the need, and the project already uses them for each metric (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml`). OpenTelemetry's SDK, through `emit()`, sends the values. The usage page of Firecrawl shows the total searches of the account, but it cannot join them with the count of unchecked items by repository, and it sends no alert. No open tool counts the items that have no alternatives check, so the Service computes that number. The change builds only three instrument declarations, one function, one rule and one dashboard row. Cost: to build, about 90,000 tokens and 5 hours of elapsed time with the CI waits (seven groups, three of them with a failing test first); to keep, about 4,000 tokens each time the check changes its selection, because `Coverage` follows `select_items`; to fix, one failing test that names the instrument, about 8,000 tokens. The change deletes no internal code.

decisions.decision: Record the two gauges in the Service row, at the start of the round, from a `Coverage` that `select_items` returns.
decisions.reason: The row calls `apply_alternatives` only `if plan.has_writes` (`run.py:616`), so a round with nothing to write would leave the last value. The start of the round also needs no guess about which writes succeed, since `apply_alternatives` skips a check when a person changed the body (`_unchanged_since_read`, `alternatives.py:871`). A gauge that is up to one round old (719 minutes) at the end of a round is enough for an alert that waits 3 days.

decisions.decision: Count an item as "with no check" when the check can take it and the job record has no check time.
decisions.reason: `_is_eligible` (`alternatives.py:483`) takes an open item with Status New or Ready and a trusted author. An item that is In Progress or from an author with no write access never gets a check, so counting it would keep the alert up for ever. An item in the retry delay has no check, so it counts, although `select_items` skips it today.

decisions.decision: Send the age gauge only when an eligible item has a check.
decisions.reason: With no check there is no age. The value 0 would read as a fresh check, and the alert on unchecked items already covers that case.

decisions.decision: Make the Service row the only sender of the two gauges.
decisions.reason: The command `devops roadmap alternatives` runs on a workstation with another `job` label, and the alert selects `job="roadmap-service"` (the rule test requires it of the group). A second sender would put a workstation value beside the Service value for one repository on the dashboard.

decisions.decision: Observe the histogram for every written check, and use `len(check.queries)` as the value.
decisions.reason: The value counts the searches that the tools ran, also a search that Firecrawl refused (`alternatives.py:259` appends before the call). A skip-class check observes 0 under `not-applicable`, and the model cannot give that verdict (`_refusal`), so the label separates the checks that could not search from the checks that did.

decisions.decision: Write the alert as `sum by (repo) (last_over_time(<gauge>[7d])) > 0 and on() (sum(<searches in 3d>) or vector(0)) == 0`, with the count of searches in the form of `_window_count`.
decisions.reason: The three parts each fix a failure that I ran in promtool 3.15.1. `sum by (repo)` and `on()` give the two sides the same label set. `or vector(0)` makes the case with no search series fire. The `_window_count` form counts the first value of a series that starts in the window; plain `increase()` fired for a new `ok` series that held 3 searches. The 7 days of `last_over_time` keep the last known gauge when the row stops, which is the failure of 2026-10-30; a gauge sample 100 hours old fires and one 180 hours old does not.

decisions.decision: Add the alert to the group `roadmap-service-activity`, and wait 1 hour.
decisions.reason: The group comment says it covers "its paid web search" (#2475), and its tests pin the rule list, so one rule joins an existing fixture file and an existing constant. The wait of 1 hour keeps one evaluation with a stale gauge from firing; the gauge changes twice a day.

decisions.decision: Put the three panels in a row "Alternatives Check" of `devops-cli.json`.
decisions.reason: The file already holds the rows of the Service's GitHub requests, and the spec `metric-instruments` already holds a panel of this dashboard ("Embedding Cache Hit Share"). #3171 edits `project-metrics.json`, so the two plans change different dashboard files and their panel ids and `gridPos` values cannot collide.

decisions.decision: Show the searches with `histogram_avg` and `histogram_count` of `increase(...[1d])`, by verdict.
decisions.reason: The existing review-duration panel reads its native histogram the same way (`devops_cli_review_duration_seconds` in `devops-cli.json`, panel 3), and `test_every_series_is_read_through_the_function_of_its_kind` accepts `increase(` for a histogram.

rejected.alternative: The alert expression of the issue, `increase(devops_cli_firecrawl_searches_total[3d]) == 0 and devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items > 0`.
rejected.evidence: I ran it in promtool 3.15.1 with the real label sets (`result="402"` on the counter, `repo="example/app"` on the gauge, 150 hours of samples). It gave no alert, because `and` needs equal label sets and the sets differ. It also reads one series per `result`, so a flat `402` series hides an `ok` search, and it returns no data when no series exists.

In promtool a new `ok` series that starts 10 hours before the evaluation and holds 3 searches gave `Labels:{alertname="Incr", repo="example/app", severity="warning"}`: a false alert. `increase()` does not count the first value of a series (#2505).

rejected.alternative: An alert on the sum of the new histogram, `histogram_sum(sum(increase(devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_searches[3d])))`, so that a search of refine does not hide a check that does not search.
rejected.evidence: The histogram gets an observation only for a written check. A round whose checks all fail after they searched writes none, which is the failure of 2026-10-30 (`raise_for_failed_checks`, `alternatives.py:918`), and the alert would then say that the check does not search. The counter sees every search. The panel "Alternatives Searches per Check" shows the checks alone, and the issue asks for the alert on any Firecrawl search.
It runs only for a plan with writes (`run.py:616`), and the check being off or having nothing to do would keep an old value.

rejected.alternative: Count every open item, or every item without the `alternatives.checked_at` mark, for the unchecked gauge.
rejected.evidence: `store.items()` holds items that the check never takes (In Progress, untrusted author). The gauge would not reach 0 and the alert would never clear.

A group needs its own fixture file, a constant and an entry in `ROADMAP_SERVICE_GROUP_TESTS` (`test_k8s_monitoring_alerting.py:78`) for one rule. The existing group has the three pieces. The cost is a MODIFIED requirement, which the spec delta carries.

rejected.alternative: Put the panels in `project-metrics.json` beside the items panels, as #3171 does.
rejected.evidence: Two plans would add panels at the same `gridPos` in one file. The Firecrawl searches are Service activity, which `devops-cli.json` already shows.
None exists on `main` (`grep -il roadmap k8s/monitoring/dashboards/*` finds no dashboard with that title), and each of those issues is open. This change would block for an unknown time.

rejected.alternative: Fix the stale path `tests/test_telemetry_instruments.py` in `instruments.py` and `generator.py` in this change.
rejected.evidence: It is a comment and a generated sentence. The change would touch the generator and the generated `docs/TELEMETRY.md` for a reason that is not the issue.

added.name: Alternatives coverage instruments are declared
added.text: `INSTRUMENTS` SHALL hold the gauge `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items` (unit `1`), the gauge `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_oldest_check_age_seconds` (unit `s`) and the histogram `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_searches` (unit `1`). The alternatives job SHALL send them through `emit()`, so the instrument check of `tests/telemetry/test_telemetry_instruments.py` covers them.

scenarios.name: The registry holds the three instruments
scenarios.then: it finds the three names with the kinds gauge, gauge and histogram, and the units `1`, `s` and `1`

added.name: The devops-cli dashboard shows the alternatives check
added.text: The devops-cli dashboard SHALL have the row "Alternatives Check" with the panels "Alternatives Unchecked Items", "Alternatives Oldest Check Age" and "Alternatives Searches per Check". Each query SHALL read its instrument through the function of its kind: a gauge through `last_over_time`, the histogram through `increase`.

scenarios.name: The queries of the three panels
scenarios.when: the panels of the row in `k8s/monitoring/dashboards/devops-cli.json` are read
scenarios.then: the queries are `sum by (repo) (last_over_time(devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items{job=~"$job"}[1d]))`, `max by (repo) (last_over_time(devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_oldest_check_age_seconds{job=~"$job"}[1d]))`, and `histogram_avg(sum by (verdict) (increase(devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_searches{job=~"$job"}[1d])))` with the count of the same selector

added.name: A round records the coverage of the check
added.text: The Service row SHALL record, once in each round and before the round writes, the gauge `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items` and the gauge `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_oldest_check_age_seconds`, with the attribute `repo`. The first counts the items that the check can take (open, Status New or Ready, trusted author) with no check, also one in the retry delay. The second is the age of the oldest check of these items. No other path SHALL record them.

scenarios.name: Six items with no check
scenarios.when: a round finds 10 items that the check can take, 4 of them with a check, and one of the other 6 failed 1 day ago
scenarios.then: the gauge `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items` records 6 for the repository

scenarios.name: An item that the check cannot take
scenarios.when: an item with no check is In Progress, and another with no check is from an author with no write access
scenarios.then: the gauge does not count either of them

scenarios.name: The oldest check is 72 hours old
scenarios.when: the oldest check of the items was written 72 hours before the round

scenarios.name: No item has a check
scenarios.when: no item that the check can take has a check
scenarios.then: the gauge of the unchecked items records the count, and the gauge of the age records no point

scenarios.name: A round with nothing to check
scenarios.when: every item that the check can take has a current check
scenarios.then: the row records the unchecked gauge 0 and the age gauge, and the model gets no request

scenarios.name: A path that is not the Service row
scenarios.when: the command runs with `--item 7`, with no `--confirm`, with `--confirm`, or on a repository where the check is off

added.name: Each written check observes its searches
added.text: For each check that it writes, the job SHALL observe the histogram `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_searches` once, with the attribute `verdict` and the number of searches that the tools of the check ran, also a search that Firecrawl refused. A skip-class check SHALL observe 0. The job SHALL observe nothing for a failed check, for a check skipped because a person changed the body, and for a plan that it does not apply.

scenarios.name: A check that searched three times
scenarios.when: the job writes a check with the verdict `none` after 3 searches
scenarios.then: the histogram has the point `{verdict="none"}` with the value 3

scenarios.name: A skip-class check
scenarios.when: the job writes the check of an item titled `docs(roadmap): a change`
scenarios.then: the histogram has the point `{verdict="not-applicable"}` with the value 0

scenarios.name: A check that is not written
scenarios.when: a check fails, a person changes the body between the read and the write, or a run only plans
scenarios.then: the histogram has no point for that item

added.name: No alternatives search with unchecked items warns
added.text: `RoadmapServiceAlternativesNotSearching` SHALL fire, by `repo`, after 1 hour in which the last value of `devops_cli_roadmap_alternatives_unchecked_items` in 7 days is above 0 and the Service has sent no Firecrawl search in 3 days, of any `result`, also when no search series exists. The count of searches SHALL add the first value of a series that starts in the 3 days. The summary SHALL name the repository and the count of items.

scenarios.name: Three days with no search
scenarios.when: `promtool test rules` evaluates a gauge of 2 for `example/app`, a `402` series that does not grow, and no `ok` series
scenarios.then: the alert fires with `repo` `example/app`, and the summary names `example/app` and 2 items

scenarios.name: No search series at all
scenarios.when: `promtool test rules` evaluates a gauge of 2 for `example/app` and no search series

scenarios.name: A search in the window
scenarios.when: `promtool test rules` evaluates a gauge of 2 and an `ok` search 1 day before the evaluation

scenarios.name: A series that starts in the window
scenarios.when: `promtool test rules` evaluates a gauge of 2 and a new `ok` series whose first value is 3, 10 hours before the evaluation

scenarios.name: No unchecked items
scenarios.when: `promtool test rules` evaluates a gauge of 0 and no search series

scenarios.name: A search of another job
scenarios.when: `promtool test rules` evaluates a gauge of 2 for `example/app` and searches of the job `devops-cli` that grow
scenarios.then: the alert fires, since the searches of a workstation do not count

scenarios.name: An old gauge
scenarios.when: `promtool test rules` evaluates a gauge whose last sample is 180 hours old, and no search series
scenarios.then: the alert stays quiet, and it fires when the last sample is 100 hours old

modified.name: The Service's activity has its own alert group

criteria.criterion: The instruments are declared and covered by the invariant that every metric is a declared instrument.
The alert rule has a promtool unit test.

dependencies: #2946 (closed, merged in #3127) gave the check its skip classes and the rule that a non-skip item searches before a verdict. It is in the tree (`src/devops_cli/roadmap/alternatives.py:557`, `skip_class_of`). Nothing to wait for. The new instruments measure its result.

#3171 (open plan of #2919) adds age gauges, one alert and a panel. Its names are different (`devops_cli_roadmap_item_age_seconds`, `devops_cli_roadmap_claim_age_seconds`) and it adds requirements only, so no requirement is in both plans. Both plans edit `INSTRUMENTS` and `__all__` in `instruments.py`, the table in `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, the rule list in `tests/prometheus/test_k8s_monitoring_alerting.py` and `k8s/README.md`. The change that merges second merges `main` and keeps both entries. Its panel goes in `project-metrics.json`, and this change uses `devops-cli.json`, so the two dashboard files do not collide.

#3174 (open plan of #2947) changes the first-pass limit of `select_items`. Its spec delta is a placeholder today. `select_items` is the function this change extends: read the merged result of #2947 before the implement step, and keep `Coverage` outside the `limit` logic.

#3069 (open) may create a dashboard `roadmap-pipeline`. #3240 and #2968 also ask for "the Roadmap dashboard", which does not exist. This change does not wait: its row moves with a one-line edit of the file name if a Roadmap dashboard exists first.

#3243 (open) would add `search_web` to the stage planner. A planner search adds to `devops_cli_firecrawl_searches_total` like a refine search does, so the alert counts it. The row panel "Alternatives Searches per Check" shows the searches of the check alone.

#2944 (open) adds the queries to the comment of a check. It reads `Check.queries`, as this change does, and writes no metric. #2951 (open) needs a verdict before Ready. Neither edits the code of this change.
security: The change adds an alert rule to `k8s/monitoring/prometheus-values.yaml` and a dashboard row to `k8s/monitoring/dashboards/devops-cli.json`. It adds no permission, no secret and no network path.
